newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed amid soy volatility, Sep down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed amid soy volatility, Sep down.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with the market underpinned by concerns about cool weather forecasts for the U.S. Midwest and a higher close in soybeans, traders said.
But thinly traded nearby September, slated for expiration at 1201 CDT Thursday, dropped in late dealings on long liquidation, they said.
Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for normal to below normal temperatures in the U.S Midwest from September 22 through September 26.

Traders said the crop needs warm weather rather than cool temperatures, to boost the maturity pace. USDA Monday said the U.S corn crop was 20 percent mature, behind the 37 percent average. USDA also said as of Sunday, the crop was 61 percent good to excellent, down from 62 percent the previous week.
Cargill Inc sold 4.5 bushels of December, LIT America sold 2.5 million December and Refco Inc bought and sold three million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn closed 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with September down 5-3/4 at $3.51-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 80,000 contracts, down from 101,363 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, bought 2,000 March $2.80 puts at 1-7/8 to two cents and Cargill Inc bought 1,000 March $2.80 puts at 1-7/8 to two cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated by USDA at 24,000 contracts, down from 32,858 Monday.
